container: Artificial intelligence can improve medicine, education, and public services, yet its influence raises difficult ethical questions. Systems trained on biased data may unfairly deny loans, jobs, or healthcare. Decisions made by opaque algorithms can be hard to challenge, especially when people cannot understand how outcomes were produced. Automation may also displace workers and concentrate wealth among companies. Meanwhile, facial recognition and predictive tools threaten privacy and can enable surveillance. Developers and governments must balance innovation with accountability, transparency, and human oversight. Responsible AI requires public participation, strong safeguards, and ways to appeal harmful decisions.
